title: Frameworks for Large Language Model Serving in HPC Environments
problem: LLM serving in HPC lacks unified frameworks for batch/interactive workloads; complexity of resource management
motivation: Growing need for LLM inference in HPC; diverse workloads require specialized scheduling and resource allocation
method: Three complementary frameworks handle different serving patterns: AI-Flux processes requests in batches for efficiency, Ray Serve responds to dynamically arriving requests, and Illinois Chat maintains always-on availability. They provide OpenAI-compatible APIs and hierarchical resource management (making resource allocation decisions at multiple levels) so users can pick the best approach for their workload type.
key_novelty: The work integrates three complementary LLM serving frameworks—batch (AI-Flux), dynamic (Ray Serve), and always-on (Illinois Chat)—using OpenAI-compatible APIs and hierarchical resource management for high-performance computing environments.
contributions: AI-Flux framework for high-throughput batch LLM inference
Ray Serve integration for dynamic interactive serving
Illinois Chat production platform for real-time LLM access
Simplified resource abstraction for HPC users
